title: Microburst detection and localization - logbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working log for investigating short high-impact latency microbursts observed in production p99/p995 for a subset of requests. The goal is to detect when a spike is a true regression vs transient load pattern, localize the root cause (model kernel, batching, network stall, KV cache miss, orchestration hiccup), and produce reproducible canary comparisons + bisect plan for rollouts.

Summary of the problem we're seeing:
- Symptom: intermittent 2-6s p99 spikes lasting ~30s-3m windows, occurring across multiple instances in a zone but not cluster-wide.
- Affected surface: hosted API route /v1/generate for model-redwood/llamaX-13B-alt, mostly with short prompts (<= 80 tokens).
- Detected by: p99 anomaly alert (dashboard rule) -> page sent at 2026-01-28 02:17 UTC.
- Immediate impact: request timeouts for some customers; autoscaling kicked but didn't reduce p99 in the short window.

Initial triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Confirm alert validity: compare dashboard p95/p99 / raw request traces. (owner)
- Check recent deploys/rollouts (last 60m). (Samir)
- Verify infra events (node reboots, kernel updates) via cloud provider console. (Ellen)
- Identify request slice: model, route, request length distribution, top customers. (Jonas)

Observed signals and quick correlations:
- Dashboard queries run:
  - PromQL (request latency):
    sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",model="llamaX-13B-alt"}[5m])) by (le) -> build histograms for p50/p95/p99.
  - Label breakdown: by instance_id, node_az, batch_size
  - Additional: gpu_utilization, cpu_steal, net_rx_err, disk_io_wait per instance
- Correlation notes:
  - Instances A,B,C in az-a experienced p99 climb; neighboring azs unchanged.
  - GPU utilization did not spike (remained 40-55%) during the microburst windows.
  - CPU sys/time shows small spike on nvidia-driver housekeeping threads on the affected hosts.
  - Container-level L7 logs show increased tail latencies but no application errors.
  - Small but clear uptick in kernel network retransmits on affected hosts during windows.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel-level network microbursts causing occasional socket stalls and delayed TCP ACKs -> latency spikes for response streaming.
2) Host-level GC/driver thread preemption (nvidia driver or CUDA context switch) causing short stalls in GPU scheduling for KV cache ops.
3) Rare older model variants being routed (quantized fallback) which have slower kernels for short sequences.
4) Autoscaler congestion: scale events cause cache misses when new instances join, leading to short p99 increase.

Experiment plan (canary + bisect):
- Canary comparison idea: create two stable routes (canary A = current baseline, canary B = same model but with network stack options changed: disable TCP offload/adjust GRO/GSO) to see if microbursts disappear under modified kernel settings. Run both under identical synthetic traffic.
- Bisect plan for recent changes: compile list of infra and runtime commits in the last 72 hours. Binary search deploys by rolling back half of commits in a test fleet and observe p99. Use canary ratio 10% test, 90% baseline.

Data collection & reproducibility steps (how to get good traces):
- Increase sampling rate for traces on route /v1/generate to 50% for next 24 hours, keep only headers and timing (privacy-safe).
- Add temporary histogram buckets to record 5ms..15s range with fine granularity around 100-1000ms, 1s..6s.
- Capture kernel-level metrics: tcp_retransmits, tcp_ack_skew, netdev_queue_drops from affected hosts using ephemeral syscalls agent.
- GPU-side: collect nvml metrics and L0 L2 stall counters for the exact 30s windows (low overhead sampling at 100ms when p99 > 800ms).
- KV cache metrics: log per-request cache hit/miss and cold-warm transitions.

Reproduction attempts so far (notes):
- Synthetic traffic replaying short prompt mix at 600 RPS produced no microbursts on isolated test fleet.
- Replaying with background noisy traffic (sporadic large embeddings requests) produced small latency tail but not the 2-6s tail.
- Replaying with toggled GRO/GSO on test nodes reproduced a modest increase in tail; turning OFF GSO reduced p99 tail on one instance. This points towards network offload interaction.

Temporary mitigations to reduce customer impact (if incident reappears):
- Route knob: pin affected customers to instances with known-good kernel settings (manual routing override).
- Autoscale cool-down: increase scale-down cool-down to avoid new instance join thrash causing cache cold starts.
- Fallback model variant: send a small fraction of traffic to a second model variant with larger batch-friendly kernels to reduce tail for short prompts.

Longer-term work items (owners + rough estimates):
- Instrumentation: add socket-level latency metrics and make them visible on per-route dashboards (Ellen, 2w).
- Kernel tuning playbook: test and document recommended GRO/GSO/TSO settings for cloud images and container isolates (Maya, Samir, 1wk).
- Autoscaler behavior audit: simulate instance churn and quantify its effect on KV cache and p99 under production load (Jonas, 3w).
- Runtime guardrail: implement detect-and-fallback if kernel retransmit spikes accompany latency spikes; explicit routing fallback to alternative nodes (eng-serving-runtime, 4w).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there other routes using the same model/micro-batched kernel combo that show the exact same time signature? (need cross-route join query)
- Can the cloud provider share NIC driver logs for the affected time windows? (submit support ticket)
- Is there any scheduled maintenance or security scanning jobs in the affected AZ that align with the timestamps?

Quick commands & queries used during triage (copyable):
- PromQL: latency histogram by instance ->
  sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",model="llamaX-13B-alt"}[5m])) by (instance_id, le)
- Host-level: check kernel retransmits ->
  watch -n 1 'ss -s; cat /proc/net/netstat | egrep "TcpExt|IpExt"'
- GPU NVML quick sample:
  python -c 'import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); h=pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0); print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetUtilizationRates(h))'
- Repro traffic runner:
  ./tools/loadgen --route /v1/generate --model llamaX-13B-alt --qps 600 --prompt-mix short-80
- Toggle GSO (test node only):
  sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off

Last timeline entries (investigation log):
- 2026-01-28 02:17 UTC: p99 alert triggered; Samir pages on-call.
- 2026-01-28 02:25 UTC: confirmed affected instances AZ-a; no deploys in last 60m.
- 2026-01-28 03:10 UTC: ran GRO/GSO toggle on one test host; p99 improved in test.
- 2026-01-30 09:40 UTC: scheduled canary experiment to run today 16:00 UTC (see linked artifacts).

Notes to self:
- Be careful: disabling GSO/GRO in prod images requires kernel boot flags for some distros; use container-level ethtool toggles in canary first.
- Retain raw kernel metrics for at least 14 days for future correlation.

Next immediate action items (today):
- Run canary A/B with GSO toggles at 16:00 UTC on a small canary pool (Samir).
- Open cloud provider support ticket for NIC driver logs (Ellen).
- Increase trace sampling to 50% for /v1/generate for next 24h (Jonas).

If you pick this up: update this log with test outcomes, attach any flamegraphs, and paste PromQL and raw traces below. Keep the timeline updated so we can produce a short postmortem if this is a regression.

-- END of logbook entry --
